caseno: Appeal from original Decree No. 165 of 1965
lawyer:
Anil Chandra Sarker -----For Appellant in F. A. No. 1 69 of 1965 and for respondent in F. A. No. 165. 
Nizamuddin Haider with A.B.M Abbasuddin -----For Respondent in F. A. No. 169 of 1965 and for Appellant in F.A. No. 165 of 1965.
parties:
Imanuddin Rarhi ----- Appellant in F A No 169 and Respondent in F.A. No. 165/65.
Vs.
Lilabati Das ----- Respondent in F.A. 169 and Appellant in F.A. No. 165/65.
full_judgment: 7. The Plaintiff may ask for relief under that section provided that the plaintiff must at the time of the suit be entitled to any legal character or to any right to any property. Section 42 must be construed strictly. The courts are only to grant such declaration which came within the terms of that section where the plaintiff has asked for a declaratory decree, namely a declaration that the decree obtained was fraudulent and void. Such a simple declaration could not be given within the provisions; of section 42 as such the suit on the face of that section has to be dismissed. In the present case we find that the plaintiff could not prove her title to the suit land although the learned Sub-ordinate Judge has found that he was in possession of the same since the passing of the ex-parte decree in his favour. Mr Sarker, the Learned Advocate has referred to a decision of this court in the case of Aminul Islam vs M/s Kilburn & Co. reported in 18 DLR 691 where it has been held that if a possessor owner is wrongfully deprived of the thing by person other than the true owner he can recover khas possession of it, after evicting the defendant from the land on the basis of possessory title even if he has not acquired any valid title. The facts of that case are completely different from the present case. In the reported case the suit was filed under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act on the averment that the plaintiff was in possession and he has been subsequently dispossessed from the suit land on encroachment by the defendant. There it was held that thought the plaintiff did not acquire any valid title, he was entitled to recover khas possession. Of course, in that case the plaintiff acquired goodwill and all interest of the original owner by virtue of an agreement. In the agreement it was stated that consideration of the goodwill and the assets of the original owner passed to the plaintiff and he would be paid by allotment of shares. In consequence of that transaction they were in possession of the suit land. It was found that the original Company validly transferred the disputed land to the plaintiff till they were dispossessed by the defendant. It was found there that the plaintiff did not acquire valid title to the suit land as no instrument of transfer was effected between the plaintiff and the original owner. But in the context it was held that plaintiff was entitled to a decree for khas possession. But in the present case the plaintiff did not file any suit for khas possession or anything of that sort and there is also nothing to show that the owners of the land transferred the suit land in favour of the plaintiff. But on the other hand, it has been found by the court below as also by us that the plaintiff could riot prove the benami nature of the document. Rather the findings of the court below are to the effect that the plaintiff went into possession of the suit land after the passing of the ex-parte decree. In that view of the matter, the decision cited by Mr Sarker is of assistance to this case. The Plaintiff has prayed for a declaration to the effect that the decree obtained by the defendant was fraudulent and collusive and not binding against the plaintiff. The plaintiff having failed to prove her title and having no legal character in the subject matter of the suit land, was not entitled to any declaration with regard to the defendant's decree to which she had no connection. If however, it transpires from the evidence on record that the decree obtained by the defendant was also tainted with the same defect as that of the plaintiff though in the present suit. We do not hold that the plaintiff was entitled of any such declaration with regard to the defendant's decree since the matter is not before us. In the interest of justice we notice that the defendant No. 1's decree was also not in accordance with law, Summons of the suit was served on a person who had no interest in the suit and admittedly the defendants of that suit were Indian citizens, but their addresses in the suit were given to be in East Pakistan. From all these the learned Sub-ordinate Judge was correct in holding that the defendant's decree also suffers from the same defect as that of the Plaintiff. However, since the plaintiff has no locus standi to challenge the same and Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari were not parties in the present suit we do not declare in the present suit the defendant's decree to be a nullify. Another factor to be noticed in the present case was that Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari were impleaded as deft. Nos. 2 and 3 in the present suit but ultimately their names were struck off. The title to the suit land remained with Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari, as such, they having not been implicated, their names having been struck off; the learned Sub-ordinate Judge has correctly dismissed the suit holding that the present suit was not maintainable in the absence of the real owners.
